Lessons.Title: End Behavior of Rational Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Calculate the end behavior of a rational function by rewriting it in the form $f(x)=q(x)+\frac{r(x)}{b(x)}$. Generalize from specific rational functions to state relationships between the end behavior and the degrees of the numerator and denominator.

To analyse a rational function p(x)/q(x), divide polynomials: f(x)=Q(x)+R(x)/q(x). If the remainder fraction approaches zero, the end behaviour follows the polynomial Q(x). Numerator and denominator degrees determine whether there is a constant, zero or nonconstant polynomial asymptote.

Source activity 19.1: Different Divisions, Revisited: Complete all three representations of the polynomial division following the forms of the integer division. \( \require{enclose} \begin{array}{r} 2x^2 \phantom{+7x+55} \\ x+1 \enclose{longdiv}{2x^3+7x^2+7x+5} \\ \end{array}\) \(2x^3+7x^2+7x+5=\) \(\dfrac{2775}{11}=252+\dfrac{3}{11}\) \(\dfrac{2x^3+7x^2+7x+5}{x+1}=\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 19.2: Combined Fuel Economy: In 2000, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) reported a combined fuel efficiency for cars that assumes 55% city driving and 45% highway driving. The expression for the combined fuel efficiency of a car that gets \(x\) mpg in the city and \(h\) mpg on the highway can be written as \(\frac{100xh}{55x+45h}\). Several conventional cars have a fuel economy for highway driving… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 19.3: Exploring End Behavior: Complete the table to explore the end behavior for rational functions. What do you notice about the end behavior of different types of rational functions? Graph \(y=j(x)\) and the line it approaches. Under what conditions would the end behavior of the graph of a rational function approach a line that is not horizontal? Create a rational function that approaches the line… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: The function \(f(x)=\frac{5x+2}{x-3}\) can be rewritten in the form \(f(x)=5+\frac{17}{x-3}\). What is the end behavior of \(y=f(x)\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Rewrite the rational function \(g(x) = \frac{x^2+7x-12}{x+2}\) in the form \(g(x) = p(x)+ \frac{r}{x+2}\), where \(p(x)\) is a polynomial and \(r\) is an integer. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Match each polynomial with its end behavior as \(x\) gets larger and larger in the positive and negative directions. (Note: Some of the answer choices are not used and some answer choices are used more than once.) \(p(x)=\dfrac{3}{x-1}\) \(q(x)=\dfrac{2x}{x-1}\) \(r(x)=\dfrac{2x+3}{x-1}\)… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Let the function \(P\) be defined by \(P(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 13x + 10\). Practice Problem 5: For the polynomial function \(f(x)=x^4+3x^3-x^2-3x\) we have \(f(\text-3)= 0, f(\text-2)=\text-6, f(\text-1)=0\), \(f(0)=0, f(1)=0,f(2)=30, f(3)=144\). Rewrite \(f(x)\) as a product of linear factors. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: There are many cones with a volume of \(60\pi\) cubic inches. The height \(h(r)\) in inches of one of these cones is a function of its radius \(r\) in inches where \(h(r)=\frac{180}{r^2}\). What is the height of one of these cones if its radius is 2 inches? What is the height of one of these cones if its radius is 3… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: A cylindrical can needs to have a volume of 10 cubic inches. There needs to be a label around the side of the can. The function \(S(r)=\frac{20}{r}\) gives the area of the label in square inches where \(r\) is the radius of the can in inches. As \(r\) gets closer and closer to 0, what does the behavior of the function… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 8: Match each rational function with a description of its end behavior as \(x\) gets larger and larger. \(\frac{99x+9}{x}\) \(\frac{99+9x}{x}\) The value of the expression gets closer and closer to 0. The value of the expression gets closer and closer to 1. The value of the expression gets closer and closer to 9. The… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
